title: evallab-outcome/1.0.0
description:
What Eval-lab emits about one evaluation run, for humans and downstream readers. Eval-lab owns this schema.

Nothing in it can express a correctness or production-safety claim. The outcome enum holds exactly four values and 'approved', 'correct', 'safe' and 'production_ready' are not among them; additionalProperties is false everywhere, so they cannot be smuggled in as extra members either. The single positive outcome, accepted_for_review, means every deterministic gate passed and a human should look -- no more than that.

no_merge_performed, no_deployment_performed and human_review_required are const true rather than booleans, because they are not outcomes of this run that could have gone the other way: they are properties of what Eval-lab is permitted to do at all. A report that could set them false would be describing a different system.

The verifier attestation appears only as a digest binding. Nothing of the verifier's internals, hidden tests or per-test results crosses into here.

schema_version.description: Pinned. An unsupported version is rejected, never reinterpreted.

bundle_id.description: The bundle this decision is about, by its producer-chosen label.

bundle_manifest_digest.description: The manifest digest of the exact bundle decided on. The label above can be reused; this cannot, so it is what ties a report to one input.

outcome.description: Exactly four values, and no others. accepted_for_review = every deterministic gate passed and a human should look. rejected = at least one deterministic gate failed. abstained = Eval-lab declined to judge, which is not a claim the work is wrong. infrastructure_failure = the harness failed, which says nothing about the work.

rationale.description: Why this outcome, in terms of the gates that produced it. Authored by Eval-lab, so it is not untrusted input -- but it is still constrained to printable text so a report cannot be made unreadable by what it quotes.

gate_results.description: The deterministic gates, in the order they ran. A decision citing no gate is a decision with no evidence behind it, so at least one is required.

scorers.description: Every rubric scorer that ran, with the versions and the model that actually answered. Empty is legitimate: a run rejected by a deterministic gate never reaches scoring.

verifier_attestation.description: A reference to the verifier's attestation, or null when no verifier was invoked. Digests and one minimal verdict only -- there is nowhere here to record a hidden test, a per-test result or a threshold, and Eval-lab must not try to infer any of them.

caveats.description: Everything that weakens this report, stated in it rather than discovered later. Non-durable execution and a mocked verifier both belong here.

durable_execution.description: False whenever the evaluation ran on the degraded local executor.

no_merge_performed.description: Eval-lab never merges. Const, because there is no path where it does.

no_deployment_performed.description: Eval-lab never deploys. Const, for the same reason.

human_review_required.description: A human remains the only authority that can accept work. True for every outcome including accepted_for_review, which is the one most likely to be misread as an approval.

gate_result.description: One deterministic gate's verdict and the artifact it read.

order.description: Execution position. JSON Schema cannot require 0..n-1 ascending; the decision policy checks that.

detail.description: What the gate read, not what it concluded about the work.

evidence_pointer.description: Optional JSON Pointer into the bundle the gate read.

scorer_record.description: What scored, at which version, with which prompt and configuration, and which model actually answered. requested_model and resolved_model are both recorded because a gateway may serve an alias with something other than what the alias names, and a score attributed to the wrong model is worse than no score.

configuration_digest.description: sha256 over the scorer's full resolved configuration, so a score cannot be reproduced against a different one by accident.

resolved_model.description: What the gateway reported having served, read back from the response rather than assumed from the alias.

attestation_digest.description: sha256 the verifier published over its own attestation record. A reference, not the record: Eval-lab stores no verifier content.

bound_jobspec_digest.description: The JobSpec digest the attestation was bound to.

bound_manifest_digest.description: The bundle manifest digest the attestation was bound to. It must equal bundle_manifest_digest above; an attestation for different bytes is a mismatch, not a pass.

verdict.description: The verifier's whole answer. 'satisfied' means the verifier's private checks were met for these exact digests -- it is not a correctness claim and does not by itself decide the outcome.
